rationale: Interpret the dedicated PreVote execution (CheckRun c72c66880fd9498ca1efb95774b0b06e, fixed experiment 381d89a2dcdc44cd95d8cc9cb5bed4cb-experiment, version 6): all five comparisons resolved - the two premises hold, the pre-step-down witness is violated, the one-tick bound holds, and the post-step-down comparison is violated because the request is no longer answered. The source prediction that PreVote alone bounds the removed leader's window the same way CheckQuorum does is therefore measured, so it moves from a reading into the account and the question's discriminator keeps only the forwarded route.

investigations.discriminator: Whether the same missing membership check produces a stale answer through the forwarded route (a follower's MsgReadIndex answered with MsgReadIndexResp), which the source reason says is not stale-productive in the single-voter shape; and whether any other membership sequence re-creates the removed leader state without the application's StepDownOnRemoval option.

interpretations.rationale: The account now covers four measured configurations of the same removal and rests on two receipts. Source side: tracker.IsSingleton is a size test whose comment asserts that the single voting member is the leader, and stepLeader's MsgReadIndex case answers locally, without a round, whenever that test holds (tracker/tracker.go:158-162, raft.go:1354-1361); the write path refuses proposals from exactly this node (raft.go:1294-1303) while the read path has no equivalent guard; and applying a committed change that removes the leading node leaves it leading under the default StepDownOnRemoval=false (raft.go:1985-2012, 282-287). Receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 measures the single-voter remainder without the quorum options (stale answer at parsed index 14 against the actual leader's committed index, control at index 4, step-down and its one-tick bound at index 15, no answer afterwards at index 16) and the two-voter remainder (no answer at all, the request held in readOnly). Receipt c72c66880fd9498ca1efb95774b0b06e measures the PreVote-only configuration on its own harness and resolves every comparison: the removal still leaves the removed leader leading a single-voter configuration (parsed index 1 holds, singleton true, is_voter false) while the new leader of {2} commits an entry it does not cover (index 2 holds), the read is answered with index 2 below that committed 4 (index 3 violated), one heartbeat tick is enough for the step-down to a follower with no leader (index 4 holds, ticks_until_stepdown 1), and the next request is not answered (index 5 violated). That last pair is what the source predicted: the step-down comes from the branch that answers a lower-term message with the receiver's term, whose guard is (checkQuorum || preVote) (raft.go:1133-1156), so either option alone bounds the window, and the measured bound is one heartbeat interval in both configurations. The defect statement is unchanged: a node that its own configuration proves is not the voter can hand a client an index that misses entries the actual leader already committed, with no confirmation round, and the exposure ends only when the removed leader learns of the new term; with two voters remaining the same missing check instead leaves an accepted request unanswerable.
counterevidence: The controls hold in the earlier receipt (parsed index 4 of 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45: the actual leader's answer covers its commit index), so answering locally is not itself the defect - the violation depends on the answering node not being the configuration's voter.

The measured bounds limit the impact: with either CheckQuorum or PreVote enabled the removed leader steps down after one heartbeat tick and stops answering (indices 15-16 of the first receipt; indices 4-5 of the PreVote receipt), and the lease-based configuration is excluded because it forces CheckQuorum.

The Node.ReadIndex contract tells callers that read index requests can be lost without notice and that retries are their duty (node.go:218-224); the two-voter shape is recorded as an accepted-but-unanswered request rather than a stale answer.

A client is expected to direct its reads at the current leader, and the library cannot generally detect that a leader is stale; what is specific here is that the local tracker already establishes that the only voter is another node while the same library refuses this node's proposals.
limitations: The scenario requires the application to apply a committed change that removes the leading node while Config.StepDownOnRemoval is false; applications that set that option, or that stop the removed node, do not reach it.

The witnesses are at the ReadIndex contract level: the receipts show the returned index below an already-committed entry with no confirmation message, and the post-step-down comparisons show the request dropped; no state machine was run, so the miss of that write in a served value is a consequence of the contract rather than a measured value.

The measured bound is one heartbeat interval in the two exercised configurations (one heartbeat tick, election timeout ten); other tick ratios, the forwarded route, and the two-voter shape with the quorum options enabled are not measured.
The lease-based negative is supported by source reading plus an incomplete native scenario, not by a retained receipt.

knowledge.assertion: IsSingleton is a size-only test over the configuration and never compares the single voter with the local node.
StepLeader answers MsgReadIndex locally whenever IsSingleton holds, using its own commit index and without a round.
A removed leader keeps leading by default while its proposals are refused and its read answers are not.
Lease-based reads force CheckQuorum, and the lease makes voters refuse higher-term vote requests while they still hear the leader.

interpretations.joint_history: Both receipts measure the same removal and read on the same fixture family (three or four voters, the application proposing and applying the removal, the removed leader keeping its leadership under the default StepDownOnRemoval=false, the new leader committing one entry, then a ReadIndex request delivered to the removed leader) with the same decisive endpoints: the returned read index compared with the new leader's commit index, the removed leader's state and the number of ticks needed to leave the leader state, and whether a later request is answered. Receipt 8090da09e0d44e13af56696a62f13d45 covers the A, B and C scenarios of one harness; receipt c72c66880fd9498ca1efb95774b0b06e is the dedicated PreVote harness whose events repeat the C scenario's shape with PreVote enabled and CheckQuorum disabled, so its indices 1-5 carry the same meaning as the corresponding events of the earlier receipt and both agree on the behaviour.
